en.title: Identical Connected Regions in Two Grids
en.description:
In each of the two 01 grids, partition the 1 cells into connected components using up/down/left/right adjacency. Count how many components in the second grid have a full coordinate set exactly equal to some full component in the first grid. This is neither a sub-island check nor a same-shape-after-translation check.

The input and output were compiled by this site.
en.input: The first line contains n m, followed by n lines of the first grid and then n lines of the second grid. Each line has m consecutive 0/1 characters. The original problem has no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n,m≤200.
en.output: A single integer, the number of exactly matching components.
en.explanation: In Example 1 only the large component matches, so the answer is 1. In Example 2 the second grid is only a proper subset of the first, so the answer is 0. In Example 3 diagonal cells are not connected, so there are two matching components.
hints: Use an iterative traversal to extract the set of cell IDs of each component, use the immutable set as a key, and count the keys of the second grid that also appear in the first grid.
